paragraphs: Allocating a resource becomes more complicated when its desirability depends on how many other people use it. This paper studies assignments in which agents care about both the resource they receive and its congestion. Its central assumption is congestion aversion: for the same resource, an agent always prefers fewer fellow users. Traffic management and school choice motivate this setting.

The authors examine a solution concept called competitiveness. Their first contribution is an algorithm that determines competitiveness in polynomial time, resolving an open question. This establishes that the competitiveness determination problem has an efficient algorithm even though preferences must account for crowding as well as resource identity.

The paper then considers finding envy-free or maximally competitive assignments while meeting individual welfare requirements called top-guarantees. Both optimization problems are proved NP-hard. The authors nevertheless develop algorithms parameterized by the number of agents or resources. These results distinguish an efficiently solvable determination problem from harder assignment searches, while identifying problem dimensions that can support more targeted algorithms.
neurips-2025-assignments-for-congestion-.tldr: The paper efficiently determines competitiveness in congestion-sensitive assignments and develops parameterized algorithms for two harder welfare-constrained assignment problems.

paragraphs: Language models can spend additional computation while answering a question by generating several possible solutions and choosing among them. This offers a way to improve reasoning without additional model training. The paper investigates why such inference-time methods can fall short in practice and benchmarks choices that affect their effectiveness across reasoning tasks.

The investigation follows the two main parts of a common pipeline: producing candidate answers and evaluating them. On the generation side, it examines instructions and sampling settings such as temperature and top-p. On the selection side, it studies self-evaluation and different reward signals. This separation matters because success depends both on generating useful candidates and on recognizing which candidates deserve selection.

Across more than 1,000 experiments involving Llama, Qwen, and Mistral models of different sizes, the proposed strategies outperform the baseline in most cases. One reported finding is that simplifying temperature choices improves general reasoning performance by up to 5%. The study shows that implementation choices that seem secondary can materially affect the value of extra inference computation.
neurips-2025-bag-of-tricks-for-inference.tldr: A broad experimental study finds that candidate-generation and reward-selection choices can substantially improve inference-time reasoning.

paragraphs: A system may have access to several kinds of sensor information during training but fewer during deployment. In collaborative settings, that mismatch interacts with another problem: individual agents may see only part of a situation. This paper addresses both issues together, with connected autonomous vehicles and cooperating robots as motivating applications.

CAML lets multiple agents collaborate and share multimodal data during training while supporting inference with reduced modalities. Its contribution is the combination of these capabilities. Existing approaches discussed in the abstract either handle missing modalities mainly for a single agent or support collaboration without addressing missing modalities at test time. CAML brings the richer training setting into a framework designed for reduced inputs during use.

In experiments on collaborative vehicle decisions in accident-prone scenarios, CAML improves accident detection by up to 58.1%. On real-world aerial-ground robot data, it improves collaborative semantic segmentation by up to 10.6% in mIoU. These findings support the framework across both event detection and scene labeling, under the evaluated conditions where training and inference have different modality availability.
neurips-2025-caml-collaborative-auxiliar.tldr: CAML trains collaborating agents with multiple modalities while allowing reduced-modality inference, improving evaluated vehicle and robot perception tasks.

paragraphs: CG-SSL learns visual representations through a progression from understanding a whole scene to identifying and matching meaningful regions. Its motivation is that two augmented views of the same image can show different object parts or scene regions. Encouraging similarity between those views alone does not explicitly account for which content they share.

Training follows three phases: encoding the overall scene, discovering visual concepts, and aligning those concepts across views. A lightweight decoder learns concept tokens by using cross-attention to gather information from image patch features. These tokens provide a way to organize visual information into distinct regions, giving the learned representation more structure and interpretability.

The concept tokens are trained through masked concept distillation and an objective that reconstructs information in feature space. The final phase uses geometry to match concept regions across heavily augmented views. This makes consistency depend on explicit regional correspondences, supporting representations that the authors describe as more compact, robust, and able to separate scene components.

Across multiple backbone sizes, the authors report state-of-the-art segmentation results when evaluating the representations with nearest-neighbor and linear probes. They also report performance approaching or exceeding leading self-supervised models trained with over 100 times more data. These findings suggest that explicitly organizing and aligning image regions can make learned features particularly useful for segmentation, where distinguishing regions is central.
neurips-2025-cg-ssl-concept-guided-self-.tldr: CG-SSL progressively discovers and aligns meaningful image regions, reporting state-of-the-art segmentation results with far less training data than some leading self-supervised models.

paragraphs: Improving a coding model involves more than getting its first answer right. Useful unit tests also let the model check and revise code during inference. This paper develops CURE, a reinforcement learning framework that jointly improves code generation and test generation without using ground-truth code solutions as supervision.

CURE trains through interactions between a coder and a unit tester, using a dedicated reward design based on their outcomes. The tester can learn from mistakes made by the coder, making those mistakes part of the training signal. This matters because conventional unit-test fine-tuning depends heavily on reference implementations, whereas CURE builds supervision from the interaction itself.

Evaluations across model sizes report strong results in both coding and test generation. The abstract gives improvements of 6.2% for test-time scaling and 25.1% for agentic unit-test generation. Its 4B model also consistently outperforms Qwen3-4B. Beyond these tasks, the authors find that a CURE model can provide effective rewards for reinforcement learning on base models without labeled supervision, extending the usefulness of the learned testing capability.
neurips-2025-co-evolving-llm-coder-and-u.tldr: CURE jointly trains coding and unit-testing abilities through reinforcement learning interactions without ground-truth code supervision.

paragraphs: Color can identify an object, convey meaning, or provide a clue needed to answer a visual question. ColorBench investigates whether vision-language models use this information effectively. It separates color understanding into perceiving colors, reasoning from color cues, and remaining reliable when colors undergo transformations, using varied scenarios grounded in applications.

The authors evaluate 32 models with different language components and vision encoders. Larger models generally perform better on this benchmark, and the language component plays a greater role than the vision encoder. Nevertheless, differences between models are relatively small. The authors interpret this limited separation as evidence that existing model development has paid insufficient attention to color understanding.

Step-by-step reasoning improves both accuracy and robustness, even though the tasks center on visual information. The evaluation also finds that models do use color clues, but those same clues can mislead them on some tasks. Together, these results show why color understanding needs several kinds of tests: using color information and using it appropriately are distinct capabilities.
neurips-2025-colorbench-can-vlms-see-and.tldr: ColorBench evaluates 32 vision-language models and finds that color cues support reasoning but can also mislead models.

paragraphs: Quantization helps accelerate large-model inference, and rotating model representations can improve it by smoothing outliers. However, learning suitable rotations through end-to-end fine-tuning can be expensive and susceptible to overfitting. DartQuant targets this calibration step, seeking useful rotations with a smaller computational burden.

The method constrains the distribution of activations after rotation. This distribution-based objective reduces the complexity of rotational optimization and its dependence on task-specific losses, which the authors connect to reduced overfitting risk. A second contribution, QR-Orth, replaces expensive alternating optimization with a more efficient scheme. Together, these changes focus on how rotations are calibrated before quantization.

Across quantization experiments, DartQuant reports superior performance. For rotational optimization on a 70-billion-parameter model, it achieves a 47-fold speedup and tenfold memory savings compared with existing methods. The authors also report completing rotational calibration for such a model on one 3090 GPU. These resource improvements concern the calibration process specifically and demonstrate a route to preparing large models for quantization with more limited hardware.
neurips-2025-dartquant-efficient-rotatio.tldr: DartQuant makes rotation calibration for LLM quantization substantially faster and less memory-intensive by optimizing activation distributions.

paragraphs: Why can a neural network fit its training examples and still perform well on unseen data? One explanation emphasizes gradient descent. The volume hypothesis proposes that good generalization could persist even with Guess & Check: repeatedly drawing random weights until finding a setting that fits the training data. This paper tests that idea theoretically in matrix factorization.

The analysis covers matrix factorization with both linear and nonlinear activation, a setting used to study neural-network behavior. The authors prove that generalization under Guess & Check worsens as width increases. This supplies a concrete case in which random search for a fitting solution is provably inferior to gradient descent, challenging a broad interpretation of the volume hypothesis.

Depth produces the opposite result: the authors prove that increasing depth improves generalization under Guess & Check, and empirically validate the width-depth contrast. The findings therefore depend on how a model is expanded. They suggest that even in relatively simple theoretical settings, the importance of gradient descent cannot be captured by one answer applying equally to width and depth.
neurips-2025-do-neural-networks-need-gra.tldr: In matrix-factorization models, random fitting generalizes worse with increasing width but better with increasing depth, complicating claims about gradient descent's necessity.

paragraphs: Electron density describes where electrons are distributed around atoms and molecules. Under the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem, it determines ground-state properties, making it a rich target for molecular modeling. Yet calculating it with density functional theory is time-consuming, and the resulting shortage of large datasets has limited its use in machine-learned force fields.

EDBench addresses this shortage with electron-density data for 3.3 million molecules, built on PCQM4Mv2. It also introduces benchmark tasks covering prediction, retrieval, and generation. This combination provides both training material and ways to assess whether models can understand and use electronic information, broadening evaluation beyond simpler targets such as energy and force.

Evaluations of several state-of-the-art methods show that learning from the dataset is feasible and can achieve high accuracy. The authors also report electron-density calculations with comparable precision and substantially lower computational cost than traditional density functional theory. They state that the data and benchmarks will be freely available, providing infrastructure for further electron-density research in drug discovery and materials science.
neurips-2025-edbench-large-scale-electro.tldr: EDBench supplies electron-density data for 3.3 million molecules and benchmarks learning methods that can reduce calculation costs.

paragraphs: GAM-Agent tackles visual reasoning by coordinating several specialized agents. Base agents handle visual perception subtasks, while a critical agent checks logical consistency and factual correctness. The framework describes their interaction as a non-zero-sum game, allowing the reasoning process to combine different contributions rather than relying on one model's uninterrupted judgment.

Agents exchange structured claims, supporting evidence, and estimates of uncertainty. An uncertainty-aware controller adjusts the collaboration and initiates additional debate rounds when agents disagree or the evidence is ambiguous. This makes disagreement an explicit signal for further reasoning. The structured exchanges also make the route to a prediction more interpretable.

Experiments on MMMU, MMBench, MVBench, and V*Bench show improvements across several vision-language backbones. The abstract reports accuracy gains of 5–6% for small-to-mid-sized models such as Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3-14B, with gains of up to 2–3% for GPT-4o. These results support the usefulness of adaptive collaboration across different model strengths, while the modular design allows the framework to organize specialized reasoning roles.
neurips-2025-gam-agent-game-theoretic-an.tldr: GAM-Agent improves visual reasoning by coordinating specialist agents and triggering further debate when uncertainty or disagreement appears.

paragraphs: This paper studies how language models' internal representations change as they work toward a multiple-choice answer. Its main lens is intrinsic dimension: a measure of the effective dimensional structure of those representations. The goal is to connect that geometry with decision-making, giving a more concrete description of otherwise opaque internal processing.

The authors examine 28 open-weight transformer models. They estimate intrinsic dimension at different layers with multiple estimators and also measure multiple-choice performance layer by layer. Combining these measurements lets them study representation geometry alongside the emergence of task-relevant predictions, rather than treating hidden-state structure as an isolated property.

Across the models, the study finds a recurring pattern: early representations have low intrinsic dimension, middle layers expand the space, and later layers compress it toward decision-relevant representations. The authors interpret this as evidence that models implicitly project linguistic inputs onto structured, low-dimensional spaces aligned with particular decisions. This is a suggested explanation grounded in the observed multiple-choice setting, offering a geometric perspective on reasoning and generalization.
neurips-2025-geometry-of-decision-making.tldr: A study of 28 language models finds that representation dimension expands in middle layers and contracts toward decision-relevant structure in later layers.

paragraphs: An autonomous-driving perception model may combine cameras, radar, and LiDAR to make a prediction. Once these inputs mix inside a network, it becomes difficult to tell which sensor contributed what. Layer-Wise Modality Decomposition, or LMD, addresses that interpretability problem by separating modality-specific information throughout an already trained fusion model.

LMD is a post-hoc, model-agnostic method, meaning its stated role is to analyze pretrained models rather than introduce a new perception architecture. Its decomposition spans all layers and attributes predictions to individual input modalities. This is useful because the question concerns how information contributes after fusion, where separate sensor streams have become entangled.

The authors evaluate camera–radar, camera–LiDAR, and three-sensor camera–radar–LiDAR systems. They assess the decompositions using structured perturbation-based metrics and visualizations separated by modality. The results support LMD's practical applicability to high-capacity fusion architectures. The contribution is a way to inspect sensor contributions to perception decisions, with evaluation across several sensor combinations used in autonomous driving.
neurips-2025-layer-wise-modality-decompo.tldr: LMD explains pretrained sensor-fusion predictions by separating camera, radar, and LiDAR contributions throughout the network.

paragraphs: A mathematical explanation can skip steps that an expert considers obvious. For a model learning from that explanation, those omissions can interrupt the connection between one reasoning step and the next. This paper calls such gaps thought leaps and studies how automatically filling them affects training and generalization.

The authors define a task that detects leaps and generates the missing intermediate steps. They build ScaleQM+ from the structured ScaleQuestMath dataset and use it to train CoT-Bridge. The resulting system enriches existing reasoning examples, making their progression more complete and coherent before those examples are used to fine-tune other models.

Across mathematical reasoning benchmarks, models trained on bridged datasets consistently outperform models trained on the originals, with gains up to 5.87% on NuminaMath. The paper also reports benefits for distilled data and for the starting point of reinforcement learning, alongside improved generalization to out-of-domain logical reasoning. These results support reasoning completeness as a useful training-data property and position CoT-Bridge as a component compatible with existing optimization techniques.
neurips-2025-mind-the-gap-bridging-thoug.tldr: CoT-Bridge fills omitted reasoning steps in training examples, improving evaluated mathematical and out-of-domain logical reasoning.

paragraphs: Continual model merging combines independently fine-tuned models in sequence without revisiting their original training data. Two difficulties arise: updates for different tasks can interfere, and incoming test data can differ from earlier distributions. This paper introduces a setting that uses a small amount of unlabeled test data during inference to address both problems.

MINGLE implements this setting with a mixture of parameter-efficient, low-rank experts. A gating mechanism controls how experts contribute, allowing adaptation while reducing conflicts. To protect earlier knowledge, gating updates are constrained to directions orthogonal to representations of previous tasks. An adaptive relaxation mechanism then adjusts the constraint strength according to observed interference, balancing preservation of earlier behavior with adaptation.

On standard continual-merging benchmarks, MINGLE reports reduced forgetting and robust generalization. It consistently exceeds previous state-of-the-art methods by 7–9% on average across different task orders. The findings support combining test-time adaptation with explicit restrictions on how new updates affect earlier tasks, under the proposed setting where a small set of unlabeled test samples is available.
neurips-2025-mingle-mixture-of-null-spac.tldr: MINGLE uses unlabeled test samples and constrained expert gating to improve sequential model merging while reducing forgetting.

paragraphs: Image generators increasingly accept both text and reference images, follow complex instructions, and preserve concepts across outputs. Existing evaluations split these abilities across separate toolkits. MMIG-Bench brings them together, covering multimodal conditioning alongside compositional meaning and common knowledge so that more of the generation task can be evaluated within one benchmark.

The dataset pairs 4,850 annotated text prompts with 1,750 reference images showing multiple views of 380 subjects. These subjects span people, animals, objects, and artistic styles. Evaluation operates at three levels: visual artifacts and identity preservation; detailed agreement between instructions and images; and aesthetics and human preference.

For the middle level, the authors introduce Aspect Matching Score, which uses visual question answering to assess fine-grained prompt-image alignment. It shows strong correlation with human judgments. The study evaluates 17 models and validates its metrics with 32,000 human ratings. This layered structure helps distinguish different sources of success or failure, making evaluation more informative than treating generated-image quality as a single undifferentiated outcome.
neurips-2025-mmig-bench-towards-comprehe.tldr: MMIG-Bench unifies multimodal image-generation evaluation with layered metrics for fidelity, instruction alignment, aesthetics, and human preference.

paragraphs: Reinforcement-learning fine-tuning can strengthen language-model reasoning, but obtaining dependable labeled training data is difficult. NaDRO addresses training with noisy or imperfect information through two complementary reward mechanisms. Its aim is to extract useful guidance even when specific scores are unreliable.

The first mechanism, Preference-based Outcome Reward, draws reliable preference signals from noisy data instead of depending on particular score values. The second, Context Perception Reward, rewards accurate qualitative assessments of the current problem state. Together, they encourage the model both to understand the situation it faces and to make a better decision within that situation.

The authors evaluate this approach in combinatorial optimization, where a model dynamically chooses heuristic algorithms. Large problem sizes and the difficulty of obtaining accurate decision data make this a relevant test of noisy-data training. Fine-tuned Qwen 7B and Llama 3-8B models outperform mainstream language models in the evaluated task. The results support the dual-reward approach for this decision setting, connecting outcome preferences with explicit assessment of context.
neurips-2025-nadro-leveraging-dual-rewar.tldr: NaDRO combines preference-based outcome rewards with rewards for understanding context to improve language-model training on noisy decision data.

paragraphs: This paper studies recovering a rank-one signal from a noisy matrix when something is already known about the signal's direction, especially a tendency toward positive entries. Ordinary spectral methods examine the observed matrix directly. The proposed nonlinear Laplacians modify its diagonal using a nonlinear function of its row sums before examining the leading eigenvalue and eigenvector.

For graph data, the row sums encode the degree profile, so this modification uses degree information to help search for unusually dense subgraphs. The authors rigorously characterize the signal strength needed for an outlier eigenvalue to emerge in studied sparse principal-component models. That threshold depends on the chosen nonlinear function, making the method tunable to the problem.

Finding the best function in closed form appears intractable, so the paper explores numerical search, learning from problem instances, and black-box threshold optimization. Both theory and experiments show substantial improvements over direct spectral methods when the function is appropriately chosen. The key qualification is this choice: the advantage comes from a suitable deformation while retaining a relatively simple spectral computation.
neurips-2025-nonlinear-laplacians-tunabl.tldr: Appropriately tuned nonlinear diagonal modifications improve spectral signal recovery when directional prior information is available.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a dynamic scene from a casually recorded monocular video requires describing both three-dimensional structure and how it changes over time. Existing Gaussian-splatting extensions often organize motion around anchors and low-rank assumptions. The paper argues that these approaches struggle with complex deformations that differ across regions of an unconstrained scene.

OriGS introduces orientation as structural guidance. It first estimates a Global Orientation Field that carries principal forward directions across space and time. It then constructs an Orientation-aware Hyper-Gaussian representation that combines time, position, geometry, and orientation within one probabilistic state. This creates a shared representation for local shape changes and broader motion direction.

Conditioned slicing of that representation infers deformation for particular regions, allowing different local dynamics to remain aligned with global motion. Experiments on challenging real-world dynamic scenes show higher reconstruction fidelity than mainstream methods. The stated contribution is therefore a way to represent varied motion more flexibly, using orientation to coordinate region-specific deformation during reconstruction from casual video.
neurips-2025-orientation-anchored-hyper-.tldr: OriGS uses orientation-guided Gaussian representations to improve dynamic-scene reconstruction from casually captured monocular videos.

paragraphs: Translating sequential programs into parallel code could make GPU programming more accessible, but suitable training data is scarce. Another difficulty is preserving what the program computes. QiMeng-MuPa addresses these issues by training a code Translator together with a Tester that generates unit tests.

The two models improve through an iterative verification-and-evolution loop. The Tester produces tests used to check and filter translated programs for functional equivalence, creating training material for the Translator. The Translator supplies translated code as additional input for improving the Tester. This connects data generation with behavioral checking, making each model's output useful to the other's learning process.

Applied to Qwen2.5-Coder, the framework reports Pass@1 improvements of up to 28.91% and a 68.90% improvement in Tester performance. It also exceeds CodeRosetta by 1.56 in BLEU and 6.92 in CodeBLEU, while achieving results comparable to DeepSeek-R1 and GPT-4.1. These experiments support mutual supervision as a way to improve sequential-to-parallel translation and testing together, with functional checking built into the training-data loop.
neurips-2025-qimeng-mupa-mutual-supervis.tldr: QiMeng-MuPa improves sequential-to-parallel code translation by having a Translator and unit-test generator iteratively train and check one another.

paragraphs: Video language models commonly answer questions with access to an entire video. Streaming use is different: an hour-long video arrives progressively, and questions may need answers before all of it has been processed. This paper proposes a training-free method that works with standard Video-LLMs to reduce the information they must retain and process.

The method uses the language model's attention to select visual tokens that contributed to understanding each short clip. It then combines hierarchical token selection with a natural-language understanding of the processed clips. Caption-based question answering supplies lightweight responses, connecting compressed visual information with textual descriptions of what has happened.

The authors report discarding up to approximately 95% of unimportant visual tokens with minimal performance loss. They also report state-of-the-art results on streaming-video benchmarks. These findings support selective retention as a practical way to balance efficiency and accuracy in the evaluated streaming setting. The contribution combines attention-informed compression with clip-level language descriptions, while requiring no additional model training.
neurips-2025-recurrent-attention-based-t.tldr: A training-free streaming-video method combines attention-based token selection and captions, discarding up to about 95% of unimportant tokens with minimal performance loss.

paragraphs: Event cameras produce asynchronous visual signals with low latency and high dynamic range. Detecting objects from these streams requires careful treatment of timing. This paper argues that methods inherited from frame-based detection often introduce temporal processing too late, while global attention can add complexity without capturing the fine temporal cues that matter.

The proposed framework combines convolutional and recurrent networks. It introduces recurrent processing early enough to preserve detailed temporal information in event-dense features. Decoupled Deformable-enhanced Recurrent Layers extract multiple spatiotemporal features using a design informed by event-camera motion characteristics. Independent downsampling across multiple scales supports flexible representations, which a feature pyramid network combines into detection outputs.

Experiments on Gen1, 1 Mpx, and eTram show higher accuracy than recent transformer-based models. These results support the paper's central architectural argument: the placement and design of temporal feature extraction can matter greatly for event-based detection. The approach demonstrates the effectiveness of recurrent, scale-aware processing in the evaluated datasets, offering a direction beyond relying primarily on global attention.
neurips-2025-rethinking-scale-aware-temp.tldr: An early, scale-aware CNN–RNN temporal encoder improves event-camera object detection over recent transformer-based models on three datasets.

paragraphs: Auditing a claimed differential-privacy guarantee involves looking for evidence that a mechanism violates it. This paper proposes a sequential statistical test for black-box mechanisms, using a stream of their outputs. The central change is that the audit can accumulate and assess evidence as outputs arrive, without committing to a fixed sample size.

The test provides anytime-valid inference while controlling Type I error: the risk of incorrectly flagging a violation. This property matters because checking results repeatedly and choosing when to stop are part of sequential auditing. The proposed procedure supplies statistical validity for that ongoing process, overcoming the fixed-batch requirement of earlier auditing methods.

Experiments across diverse realistic mechanisms show violations detected with far fewer samples, reducing requirements from 50,000 to a few hundred in the reported comparisons. The method also identifies privacy violations in DP-SGD in less than one training run, whereas prior methods require full model training. These findings demonstrate substantial empirical savings in evidence collection and earlier detection during the evaluated training setting.
neurips-2025-sequentially-auditing-diffe.tldr: A sequential privacy audit controls false alarms while detecting evaluated violations with far fewer samples and sometimes before one training run finishes.

paragraphs: Adapting vision-language models usually requires backpropagation and access to gradients, which creates difficulties on memory-constrained devices designed for inference. Forward-only optimization avoids that requirement, but existing evolutionary and zeroth-order approaches can suffer from high variance and weak performance. SharpZO improves this adaptation process through a two-stage optimization design.

The first stage uses a sharpness-aware evolutionary strategy to explore broadly and smooth the loss landscape, creating a stronger initialization. The second stage applies sparse zeroth-order optimization for more detailed local search. Both stages use only forward passes. The design connects a broad warm-up phase with a focused refinement phase so that local optimization starts from a more favorable position.

The paper combines theoretical analysis with experiments on CLIP models. It reports improvements in both accuracy and convergence speed, including up to a 7% average gain over state-of-the-art forward-only methods. These findings support the staged approach for vision-language prompt tuning when gradient-based adaptation is unavailable, with sharpness-aware initialization contributing to subsequent forward-only refinement.
neurips-2025-sharpzo-hybrid-sharpness-aw.tldr: SharpZO combines sharpness-aware evolutionary warm-up with sparse local optimization to improve vision-language prompt tuning using only forward passes.

paragraphs: Learning from expert demonstrations can avoid manually specifying a reward, but matching actions at individual states may miss the coherence of a long sequence. This paper instead aims to learn a policy that maximizes the probability of producing expert-labeled trajectories. The objective makes whole-trajectory behavior central to learning.

The authors prove that the general trajectory-alignment problem is NP-complete. Trajectory Graph Learning addresses this difficulty under structural assumptions, including bounded realizability of expert trajectories or a tree-structured decision process. Under the relevant assumptions and with known dynamics, its graph-based planning algorithm computes optimal policies in polynomial time. Those conditions are essential to the stated tractability result.

For unknown dynamics, the paper develops an algorithm using upper-confidence-bound-style exploration and establishes sublinear regret. Grid-world experiments show substantial improvements over standard imitation-learning methods for planning long trajectories. The contribution joins a direct trajectory objective with structural conditions that make planning manageable, then extends the approach to learning when the environment's dynamics are initially unknown.
neurips-2025-trajectory-graph-learning-a.tldr: Trajectory Graph Learning directly aligns policies with expert trajectories, with efficient optimal planning under stated structural assumptions and known dynamics.

paragraphs: Autoregressive image models generate images through next-token prediction, a paradigm originally developed for language. This paper investigates why that training objective can struggle to build high-level visual understanding. It identifies three obstacles: local and conditional dependence, inconsistent semantics between generation steps, and insufficient spatial invariance.

The authors introduce Self-guided Training for AutoRegressive models, or ST-AR, to address these obstacles with self-supervised training objectives. The framework improves visual representations without relying on a separate pretrained representation model. Its central idea is to strengthen the model's understanding during training so that the representations supporting generation carry more useful visual meaning.

The experiments show improved image understanding together with better generation quality. ST-AR reports approximately 42% FID improvement for LlamaGen-L and 49% for LlamaGen-XL while keeping the sampling strategy unchanged. That unchanged sampling strategy ties the reported gains to the training framework rather than a different generation procedure. The findings support self-supervised representation learning as a useful addition to autoregressive image-model training.
neurips-2025-understand-before-you-gener.tldr: ST-AR adds self-supervised training objectives to improve autoregressive image understanding and generation without pretrained representation models.
